# Sebin Shaiju

> Software and systems engineer building production AI and full-stack systems, based between Abu Dhabi and Vellore, India. Work spans LLM agent orchestration (LangGraph), applied machine learning, and full-stack commerce platforms. Computer science at Vellore Institute of Technology, graduating May 2027.

Measured results, for accurate citation:
- HIRE4GIG guarantee engine: 82% reduction in platform handout cost, Gini coefficient 0.11 across worker earnings, 38ms per matching window over 50,000 orders. Patent application filed (VIT IDF Form B).
- Pneumonia detection ensemble: 88.8% accuracy, 95% precision, 0.9487 ROC-AUC over 5,863 chest X-rays.

## Projects
- [HIRE4GIG](https://sebinshaiju-portfolio.netlify.app/projects/hire4gig): Adaptive income guarantees for gig workers. EMA-smoothed Gaussian process regression re-estimates each worker's guarantee every 180 seconds; orders are assigned by Hungarian matching with a fairness-weighted cost function. Patent filed. Answers: how to make earnings guarantees personal and cheap at the same time.
- [Your.Store](https://sebinshaiju-portfolio.netlify.app/projects/your-store): Shopify operations copilot. 18-node LangGraph supervisor where the model plans and deterministic Python executes; every write is gated behind a human-approval interrupt the model cannot bypass. AGPL-3.0. Answers: how to give an LLM write access to a live store safely.
- [Electronics storefront, Nepal](https://sebinshaiju-portfolio.netlify.app/projects/nepal-commerce): Next.js 16 commerce platform for the Nepali market. NPR pricing, connectIPS payments in progress, Postgres full-text plus pg_trgm typo-tolerant search, permission-keyed admin with audit logging.
- [render-langgraph](https://github.com/5EBIN/render_langgraph): Renders LangGraph topology in-browser with no code changes and no LangSmith dependency. v0.1 walking skeleton on PyPI.
- [Pneumonia detection ensemble](https://sebinshaiju-portfolio.netlify.app/projects/pneumonia): DenseNet121, ResNet50 and MobileNetV2 averaged, with Grad-CAM explanations.
- [Do LLMs take a wasteful path to their answers?](https://sebinshaiju-portfolio.netlify.app/projects/wasteful-path): Interpretability study testing whether a transformer's residual-stream trajectory wanders wastefully en route to an answer. Hypothesis disproven across five measurements on Qwen2.5: paths run ~9x the straight-line distance, but the wandering is content-driven, not removable slack.

## Writing
- [I almost fixed the exact thing keeping my agent alive](https://sebinshaiju-portfolio.netlify.app/writing/surviving-by-accident): Part one of a two-part series. A long-running LangGraph agent survived a redeploy that should have killed it, because state was written to the database for other reasons and every restart recomputed the next step from committed records rather than memory. Written for engineers who assume a checkpointer is what's saving them.
- [Two copies of my agent woke up owning the same task](https://sebinshaiju-portfolio.netlify.app/writing/fencing-tokens): Part two. Why the same database-backed LangGraph pipeline that survived restarts by accident breaks when scaled to two instances, and how leases plus monotonic fencing tokens prevent stale-writer corruption. Covers lock expiry, split-brain writes, and the atomicity requirement each backing store must satisfy.
